channel.title: Said & Checked — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, 2026-11-20: none false or contradicted, 2 unsupported, 8 unsettled (Donald Trump)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported and Unsettled

  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “Reported as: He reiterated Thursday that he and Xi agree Iran needs to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for world energy supplies that has become a chokepoint since the start of the war.” Unsupported. No Chinese record found states or rejects that Iran must fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz; the statement rests on Trump's own account. Searched: China's Foreign Ministry readouts of the Nov. 19 summit and bilateral meeting (which mention only that the Middle East was discussed), the joint declaration, and AP's report; Xinhua could not be loaded, and no Chinese-language record was searched.
  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “Reported as: They also agree that Iran cannot obtain a nuclear weapon, Trump said.” Unsupported. No Chinese record found says China agrees Iran cannot obtain a nuclear weapon. China's summit readout and the joint declaration speak of preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons in general and do not name Iran. Searched: the two Chinese Foreign Ministry readouts of Nov. 19, the joint declaration and AP's report; Xinhua could not be loaded, and no Chinese-language record was searched.
  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “Reported as: Trump said they had a shared interest in having oil flow through the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for oil shipments from the Middle East that was repeatedly shut because of attacks in the Iran war.” Unsettled. China's Foreign Ministry readouts of the Nov. 19 trilateral summit and of the Xi-Trump meeting do not mention Hormuz, oil shipments or Iran; they say only that the Middle East situation was discussed. The joint declaration released by the White House says the three countries "reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows", which is general and does not decide the specific Hormuz point.

item.title: Said & Checked, 2026-11-19: 1 contradicted (Markwayne Mullin)
item.description:
False or contradicted

  • Markwayne Mullin, Secretary of Homeland Security: “We landed over 4,000 planes when the ground stoppage went out because of the communication and didn't have one single incident.” Contradicted. The FAA's Nov. 15 Q&A says "approximately 3,500 aircraft safely landed" when the ground stop was implemented, below the more than 4,000 stated, and that every passenger arrived safely. The FAA figure is approximate, and the FAA and L3Harris investigation into the root cause is still open.

Disagreements

  • Markwayne Mullin, Secretary of Homeland Security: “If we canceled something with the airspace completely open, it could bring confusion” (premise supported)
    Bennie Thompson, U.S. Representative from Mississippi: “For the secretary of homeland security to do that during a crisis was not only irresponsible, Mr. Secretary, but also incredibly tone-deaf.”
    Both statements in context
  • John Cornyn, U.S. Senator from Texas: “there's better qualified people to hold that job”
    Ted Cruz, U.S. Senator from Texas: “If the Senate Judiciary Committee does not move Gaiser forward, the people of Texas will pay the price because it will effectively give the judicial seat to the Democrats, who will keep it vacant in perpetuity”
    Both statements in context

item.title: Said & Checked, 2026-11-18: 2 contradicted (Melanie Stansbury, Darrell Issa)
item.description:
False or contradicted

  • Melanie Stansbury, U.S. Representative from New Mexico: “Cormorants have been protected under the Migratory Bird Treaty Act for over 100 years.” Contradicted. The Fish and Wildlife Service's 2003 Federal Register rule, read in the check, says double-crested cormorants 'have been protected under the MBTA since 1972', through the 1972 amendment to the 1936 U.S.-Mexico convention; that is 54 years, not over 100. The rule could not be read directly by the editor, so the result is held at contradicted rather than false.
  • Darrell Issa, U.S. Representative from California: “Currently the Bureau of Land Management spends a not insignificant number of dollars every year and growing maintaining 847 acres of land that earns no money” Contradicted. The text of H.R. 8483 in the Congressional Record divides the approximately 847 acres into about 164 acres of Bureau of Land Management land ('Parcel 1') and about 683 acres of Forest Service land ('Parcels 2 and 3'), so BLM does not manage all 847 acres. The total acreage matches. The record gives no revenue or maintenance-cost figures, so 'earns no money' was not tested.

Disagreements

  • Sean Duffy, Secretary of Transportation: “Reported as: He again reiterated that it is was a faulty router made by Juniper Networks that was to blame.” (unsettled)
    Suhas Subramanyam, U.S. Representative from Virginia: “the FAA problem that occurred on Friday was actually a configuration issue.” (unsettled)
    Both statements in context
  • Melanie Stansbury, U.S. Representative from New Mexico: “This bill would undermine the Clean Water Act, the National Environmental Policy Act, and the Endangered Species Act, bedrock environmental” (unsettled)
    Alan Armstrong, U.S. Senator from Oklahoma: “it does not compromise our environmental protections” (unsettled)
    Both statements in context
  • Bruce Westerman, U.S. Representative from Arkansas: “Double-crested cormorants have recovered significantly since their listing under the Migratory Bird Treaty Act in 1972.” (supported)
    Melanie Stansbury, U.S. Representative from New Mexico: “Cormorants have been protected under the Migratory Bird Treaty Act for over 100 years.” (contradicted)
    Both statements in context

item.title: Said & Checked, 2026-11-17: 2 contradicted (Michael Bennet)
item.description:
False or contradicted

  • Michael Bennet, U.S. Senator from Colorado: “the Iran war that is so deeply unpopular with the American people whether they are Republicans or Democrats.” Contradicted. The Economist/YouGov poll of April 3-6, 2026 found 34 percent of Americans supporting the war and 53 percent opposed, with Democrats 9 to 84 against but Republicans 67 to 21 in favor. A post-election YouGov survey found 62 percent of 2026 voters calling the war the wrong decision; no current party breakdown was found, so whether Republican support has since fallen below a majority remains open.
  • Michael Bennet, U.S. Senator from Colorado: “In fact, most of them are taking home even less than they ever have.” Contradicted. USDA's Economic Research Service forecasts 2026 net farm income at $158.4 billion, above its 2006-25 average after inflation, and AskAmerica's ERS data show average net cash income per farm of $56,600 in 2025, about double 2010; the lowest-income group, residence farms, was not at a record low. One group, intermediate farms, hit a series low in 2024; farm household income was not read, and the 2025-26 figures are estimates and forecasts.

Disagreements

  • Sean Duffy, Secretary of Transportation: “I have no money in that $12.5 billion that I can use for a new architecture for telecom.” (unsettled)
    Jim Himes, U.S. Representative from Connecticut: “that's sitting in your bank account right now?” (premise unsettled)
    Both statements in context
  • John Thune, U.S. Senator from South Dakota (Senate Majority Leader): “It took a year and a half before Democrats finally let a few nominees go by voice vote--something no other President has had to deal with.” (unsettled)
    Dick Durbin, U.S. Senator from Illinois: “He determined that he would not allow any U.S. attorney to go forward under Joe Biden without a rollcall vote.” (unsettled)
    Both statements in context

item.title: Said & Checked, 2026-11-16: none false or contradicted, 4 unsettled (Donald Trump, Pete Hegseth)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “It is in a terrible state of disrepair, as anybody can see by just looking at the pictures that are now circulating all over the Country, and in the Court” Unsettled. FOX 5 DC reports that a court filing by the superintendent of the National Mall and Memorial Parks says the former operator did not keep up agreed maintenance and found several areas of the course "to either be deteriorating or needing work". The filing itself could not be read directly, and no National Park Service condition assessment or deferred-maintenance figure for the course was found. Whether that amounts to a "terrible state of disrepair" is a judgment the record read does not settle.
  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “They don't call it Trash Island for no reason!” Unsettled. City Cast DC reports that, according to an Oct. 9 Washington Post story, National Park Service crews had used the name for "an overgrown central area of debris and invasive vegetation" in the park; that Post story could not be read directly. City Cast also reports that the D.C. Public Library's People's Archive "did not find a record where East Potomac Park had been referred to as 'Trash Island'" and that a search of the Post's archive found no earlier use of the name for the park. Only the name was checked.
  • Pete Hegseth, U.S. Secretary of Defense: “Every once in a while you might have one, unfortunately we call it a squirter that makes its way through.” Unsettled. No official count of how many Iranian drones and missiles got past U.S. defenses in the war's first days was found. At the same briefing the chairman of the Joint Chiefs said U.S. systems had "intercepted hundreds of ballistic missiles"; launch totals attributed to the head of U.S. Central Command (more than 2,000 drones and 500 ballistic missiles, as reported by DefenseScoop) come with no matching intercept count. Defense Department pages refused the fetch, so the briefing was read from a copy of the transcript.

item.title: Said & Checked, 2026-11-15: 1 false, 3 contradicted (Chris Van Hollen, Sean Duffy)
item.description:
False or contradicted

  • Chris Van Hollen, U.S. Senator from Maryland: “And I chair the subcommittee that oversees the Department of Commerce that helped expose his involvement with the -- with Epstein.” False. The Senate Appropriations Committee's own page for its Commerce, Justice, Science subcommittee lists Jerry Moran as chair and Chris Van Hollen as ranking member, and AskAmerica's committee roster shows the same. Republicans hold the Senate majority until the new Congress is seated in January. The second part of the sentence, on what the subcommittee helped expose, was not checked: no page read addressed it.
  • Sean Duffy, U.S. Secretary of Transportation: “Reported as: He has said the problem began when L3Harris was replacing a section of old copper wire with new fiber wire, somehow causing the system to overload.” Contradicted. The FAA's published account says otherwise. Asked whether upgrades caused the outage, it answers no and attributes the instability to the legacy system. It says data from two sites, a radar site in Amarillo, Texas and a radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, where L3Harris had deployed a new router, flooded the network. The FAA also says the root cause is still under investigation, and L3Harris has not named a cause. The wording checked is AP's account of what the secretary said.
  • Sean Duffy, U.S. Secretary of Transportation: “They gave me money for tower -- for radios, money for radar, money for systems. But I don't have any money in that $12.5 billion for a new architecture for telecom.” Contradicted. Section 40003(a)(1) of Public Law 119-21 appropriates $4,750,000,000 "for telecommunications infrastructure modernization and systems upgrades", the largest single item in the $12.5 billion. Still open: whether that item can pay for a wholly new telecommunications architecture, as distinct from upgrades; the law's text does not say.
  • Chris Van Hollen, U.S. Senator from Maryland: “Republicans in Washington raised twice as many funds.” Contradicted. AskAmerica's Federal Election Commission data for the 2026 cycle show the three Republican national party committees with receipts of $843.1 million (RNC $341.5 million, NRCC $263.8 million, NRSC $237.8 million) against $725.5 million for the three Democratic committees (DNC $252.3 million, DCCC $256.8 million, DSCC $216.4 million): about 16 percent more, not twice. The FEC's own 18-month summary gives the same ratio. Still open: super PACs and other outside groups, which were not counted.

Contradictions and Disagreements

  • Contradicts own statement.
    Sean Duffy, U.S. Secretary of Transportation: “So we were forced by the telecom provider to actually update that copper to fiber, and we brought in our routers and did the work.” (unsettled)
    Sean Duffy, U.S. Secretary of Transportation: “There was an old fiber line that was going to be decommissioned by our telecom provider.” (unsettled)
    Both statements in context
  • Cory Booker, U.S. Senator from New Jersey: “And now he just wants to walk away.”
    Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State: “The economic pain that we are inflicting on that regime is so great that there's no need for military action because we've weakened them so much,” (premise unsettled)
    Both statements in context
  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “old and broken system worse than when they began”
    Sean Duffy, U.S. Secretary of Transportation: “And I can't blame Republicans or Democrats, because it's all of them.” (premise supported)
    Both statements in context
  • Sean Duffy, U.S. Secretary of Transportation: “So all that money hasn't been spent, but it's been obligated to radar.” (unsettled)
    Jim Himes, U.S. Representative from Connecticut: “This is not a Congress money problem. You pointed out that there was $50 billion sent in the Biden administration and $12.5 billion appropriated that has not been obligated.” (unsettled)
    Both statements in context
